name: All Saints
tagline: The saints the world forgot. Heaven didn't.
mission: Daily one-minute lives of lesser-known saints, told with reverence, on their feast day.

colorRoles.accentMartyr: martyr (martyrs only: thin rule under name)

display.use: Saint names, title cards, monogram. Always uppercase, tracking +12%.

text.use: Captions and on-screen lines. SemiBold 600 for captions.

accent.use: Quotes, the devotional close, feast-day line.

motion.artMove: Slow push-in or drift, 4-8% scale over a scene. Never fast zooms, never shake.
motion.transitions: Cross-dissolve 0.6s or dip-to-soot 0.4s. No swipes, spins, or glitch effects.
motion.lightLeak: Subtle warm candle flicker vignette, opacity under 15%.
motion.grain: Fine film grain, 4% opacity, for a unified look across different paintings.

gemini.profile: The Master Storyteller. A warm, deep, unhurried male narrator telling the lives of the saints.
gemini.scene: A quiet church at dusk. One candle. He speaks to a single listener.
gemini.notes: Reverent, never theatrical. Unhurried but moving, with only brief pauses between sentences. Say the names of people and places carefully and clearly.

beats.hook: Quiet intrigue: draw the listener in, as if sharing something remarkable.
beats.who: Plain and grounded, introducing a person and a place.
beats.story: Steady storytelling; let each image land.
beats.turn: Softer and slower; this is the heart of it.
beats.close: Prayerful and gentle, slightly slower, with a brief pause before 'pray for us'.

voice.narrator: Warm, deep male. Unhurried (about 140 words per minute). Reverent, never preachy or sensational.

structure: HOOK (1 sentence, under 14 words): the single most arresting true detail of their life.
WHO: name, era, place in one breath.
STORY: 3-4 beats, concrete and visual. One idea per sentence.
TURN: what their holiness looked like in practice.
CLOSE: one line of meaning for today, then 'Saint ___, pray for us.'
rules: Accuracy over drama. Separate history from tradition: use 'tradition holds' / 'according to legend' for unverified miracles and martyrdom details.
Use 'Saint' only for canonized saints or pre-congregation saints venerated as such; use 'Blessed' / 'Venerable' correctly.
Reverent, warm, plain words. No slang, no clickbait ('you won't believe'), no sarcasm.
Avoid graphic description of martyrdom; name it with dignity.
Never contradict Catholic teaching; never speculate about a saint's private sins beyond the historical record.
Pronunciation: spell unusual names phonetically in the TTS line if needed.

illustration.style: Painted as a traditional Byzantine icon: egg tempera on a wooden panel, burnished gold-leaf background, flat stylized figures with bold dark outlines, elongated proportions, inverse perspective, symbolic simplified architecture and landscape, solemn non-naturalistic faces with large calm eyes, deep reds, ultramarine and ochre, subtle craquelure and aged patina. Reverent and devotional. Vertical composition. The painting fills the entire image edge to edge: no panel edge, no border, no frame. No text, no letters, no inscriptions.
illustration.setting_rule: Architecture, clothing, armor and landscape must be authentic to {region} in the saint's era ({dates}), not generic European.
illustration.consistency: Keep it strictly iconographic (flat, gilded, stylized), never a naturalistic oil painting. Dress each figure exactly as the scene says; keep a religious habit's colors consistent with the order named (e.g. Dominicans: white habit and black cape).
